text:
[Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) refines importance-corrected sampled softmax: the positive is always present, so treating it as sampled from the negative proposal introduces error. Its revised gradient uses correction over negatives and a stop-gradient uncertainty weight. This addresses sampling-distribution bias, not false-negative identification; transferring its objective to masked BERT4Rec remains an experimental hypothesis. [gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) separately shows that sampled BCE can cause overconfidence and unstable training—evidence for investigating the objective without changing the BERT4Rec backbone.

[R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) identifies problems with immediate hardest-negative mining: early training failure, limited candidate coverage, and uncontrolled difficulty. It uses uniform warm-up, efficient approximate global recall, then curriculum-based negative selection. This supports testing gradual hardness rather than deterministic top-1 mining, but does not establish false-negative immunity. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), an older direct treatment of false negatives, uses teacher-generated soft labels; that teacher/student recipe falls outside this experiment’s single-model constraint.

Practical hypothesis: retain one masked BERT4Rec per category; compare a multi-negative sampled-softmax objective against the baseline, then separately test uniform warm-up plus stochastic semi-hard sampling. Exclude target collisions and observed training positives from negative pools; unobserved items remain uncertain negatives. Importance correction must match the actual proposal—top-k mining cannot simply inherit uniform-sampling correction. Keep terminal-mask allocation fixed during these comparisons. Select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; stronger training margins alone provide no evidence of gains in Electronics or Industrial_and_Scientific.
